lines.text: Many learners say: I have a date with the dentist.
Better: I have an appointment with the dentist.
A date is romantic. Use appointment.
An appointment! I have an appointment with the dentist.

data.wrong: I have a date with the dentist.
data.right: I have an appointment with the dentist.
data.why: A date is romantic. Use appointment.

native.tip: En español “cita” sirve para todo, pero “date” en inglés es una cita romántica: con el dentista, “appointment.”
native.caption: 🙈 Error común: “I have a date with the dentist.” “Cita” con el médico no es “date”: “I have an appointment with the dentist.” ¡Escucha a Carlos y repite! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “an appointment”. Para el médico o el dentista usa “appointment”; “date” es una cita de pareja. Escribe una frase tuya con “an appointment” o dila en voz alta: {link}

en.tip: Learners use “cita” for everything, but a “date” is romantic. For a dentist, say “appointment.”
en.caption: Common mistake: “I have a date with the dentist.” A doctor’s “cita” is not a “date”: “I have an appointment with the dentist.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
